blocks.title: The big idea
blocks.body: A recursive function solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller version. It needs a base case that stops it and a recursive case that moves toward it.

blocks.title: Checklist
items: Is there a base case that returns directly?
Does every call get closer to the base case?
Trust the smaller call to be correct

blocks.title: Base and recursive case
Facts to remember
items: 5! is 120 and 12! fits in an int, 13! does not
fib(10) is 55; naive fib(10) makes 177 calls
A missing base case usually crashes the program

blocks.title: Divide and conquer
items: Divide the problem into smaller pieces
Conquer each piece with the same method

blocks.body: Use a loop when it is just as clear. Use recursion when the problem splits into smaller copies of itself.
